data.turoyo: Komər kḥoyər: kale əxtiyar w kətle daqno. Komər tamo komər ǧʕəkle
data.translation: Als er sah, daß er einen alten Mann mit einem Bart vor sich hatte, kroch er auf den Knieen

rationale: Thin I Preterit cell, with two existing elicited examples; this first supplied narrative attestation gives independently understandable motivation and retains the edition's German wording.

summary: 99/53 provides narrative I Preterit ǧʕəkle alongside the existing Ilyas p.c. examples. The moving participant is expressed through the l-series despite no overt object; no transitive sense or Detransitive interpretation is required.

The old man's appearance and the ensuing Oheim/Vater address explain deference. Crawling remains physical motion; the German edition's on-the-knees specification is retained without adding kneeling or submission as a separate sense.
The English inherited gloss to crawl, creep and unknown-etymology heading remain unchanged. The German edition translation is quoted in its original language.
Does ǧʕəkle denote crawling on the knees specifically in 99/53, or general crawling performed deferentially? One narrative token does not establish a separate kneeling sense.
